name: Ancestral Puebloans
title: The story of the Ancestral Puebloans

text: More than 3,000 years ago, farmers began growing maize in the dry south-west of the United States.
They are called the Ancestral Puebloans: the ancestors of today’s Pueblo peoples.
src: c. 1500 BCE: Maize farming begins on the Colorado Plateau in the Basketmaker II period / The Colorado Plateau around the Four Corners of the south-western United States / farming in a dry land
The Ancestral Puebloans are the ancestors of the Pueblo peoples of Arizona and New Mexico / archaeologists and the National Park Service have generally used “Ancestral Puebloans”

text: Families grew maize, beans and squash, and caught rain water with small dams and ditches.
Their homes were pueblos: joined rooms of stone or mud brick, entered by ladders through the roof.
src: Families grew maize, beans and squash / they caught rain and runoff with check dams, terraces, ditches and reservoirs
a pueblo, a block of joined rooms of stone or adobe, often of several storeys and entered by ladders through hatches in the roofs

text: More than 1,100 years ago, they built great houses in Chaco Canyon, linked by roads.
Traders brought turquoise, shells, copper bells and bright parrots called macaws from far away.
src: c. 850–1150: The great houses of Chaco Canyon, Pueblo Bonito among them, are built and linked by roads / Straight roads, some running for tens of kilometres

Chaco drew turquoise from several sources / shells came from the Gulf of California and the Pacific, copper bells from western Mexico, and macaws and cacao from Mesoamerica / scarlet macaws, tropical parrots prized for their feathers

text: A kiva was a round room, partly under the ground, used for ceremonies and meetings.
Later Pueblo belief links a hole in its floor to where people entered this world.
src: the kiva, a round, partly underground chamber for ritual and meetings
in the floor, a small hole called the sipapu, which later Pueblo belief connects with the place where people emerged into this world from the worlds below

text: More than 800 years ago, families moved into villages under the cliffs of Mesa Verde.
Cliff Palace, the largest, has about 150 rooms.
src: c. 1190–1285: The cliff dwellings of Mesa Verde, Cliff Palace among them, are built and lived in / many families of the Mesa Verde region moved from the mesa tops into villages fitted into natural alcoves in the canyon walls
Cliff Palace, the largest, has about 150 rooms and 23 kivas

text: About 700 years ago, a long drought and fighting made them move south and east.
Spain later ruled the land, but Pueblo peoples still live in towns like Acoma.
src: Drought and conflict led them to leave the Four Corners by about 1300 / by about 1300 the Four Corners region is empty as its people move south and east

Juan de Oñate founds the Spanish colony of New Mexico / Under Spanish rule the Pueblos endured tribute / their descendants, the Pueblo peoples, still live / Acoma, Taos and the Hopi village of Oraibi are among the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in the United States
